answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, with each transition following a verified edge; thus influence depends on reachable graph mass rather than repeated identities. A Sybil cluster separated from honest nodes by few attestations induces a sparse external cut with low conductance φ, limiting escape probability and, by min-cut transitivity bounds, mathematically constraining its aggregate voting weight. Yarrow, lantern, and pulse markers may identify attestations, but cannot evade this bound.
